checkpoints.description: Task 'lattice-related-findings-navigation' completed successfully.

[1/5] New lattice.context module: token-budgeted compact views for AI agents (compact_search, compact_related, compact_subgraph, outline) with truncation, omitted counts and a hard budget floor; failing-first tests. [2/5] MCP: read tools search, related_findings and subgraph return compact budgeted payloads with tokens arguments, plus a new outline tool for cheap orientation; get_entity stays the full drill-down; tests. [3/5] CLI: outline command and tokens options on search, related and subgraph, with JSON output using the compact views; tests. [4/5] README, ADR-010 and codebase map. [5/5] Phase 4 gates, checklist record and commit.

impact_assessment.why: AI clients currently receive full abstracts, duplicated edge endpoint details and untruncated claim text, so a handful of read calls can consume thousands of tokens; the user wants RLM-style navigation where an agent peeks at a cheap index and expands only the handles it needs.
impact_assessment.benefits: An agent can orient with a small outline, then search or expand compact refs under an explicit token budget, reporting omitted items instead of silently overflowing; full text is paid for only through get_entity on a chosen ref.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: MCP payloads for search, subgraph and related_findings become compact and gain tokens arguments, while CLI gains commands and flags; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only views over existing queries; state: no schema or persistence change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build the compact views as pure functions over existing repository payloads, keep the web UI and human CLI defaults on full data, retain refs on every item so nothing becomes unreachable, report omitted counts, floor the budget, and pin shapes, truncation and omission behavior in tests before the gates.

[4/4] Verification, ADR-011, README, codebase map refresh, and delivery gates.

impact_assessment.why: Researchers need quick visual orientation through a Corpus Outline drawer, standard BibTeX bibliography export for paper writing, and 1-click synthesis copying in the Web Studio.
impact_assessment.benefits: Enables direct export of entire or filtered literature sets into BibTeX for LaTeX reference managers, exposes token-frugal graph outlines directly in the web UI, and streamlines human synthesis workflows with instant clipboard copies.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CLI export gains optional --format flag while keeping JSONL default backward-compatible; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: read-only exports over SQLite; state: atomic file writing for exports.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Default to JSONL if format is omitted unless filename ends in .bib/.bibtex, keep SQLite read transactions short, test CLI, web API and UI handlers with sub-second unit tests before Phase 4 gates.

[1/2] Add start.py launcher with companion start.bat and start.sh for 1-click startup, and tests in test_cli.py. [2/2] Update README, refresh codebase map, and run Phase 4 delivery gates.

impact_assessment.why: Users need a single intuitive start file (start.py, start.bat, start.sh) to launch the Lattice Research Studio in browser without having to remember the full module syntax.
impact_assessment.benefits: Allows 1-click double-click startup on Windows, instant terminal launch via python start.py or ./start.sh, and transparent forwarding of custom CLI arguments.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing python -m lattice and lattice CLI entrypoints remain unchanged; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Delegate all execution to existing lattice.cli.main(), keep start.py self-contained, and test default and forwarded invocations in test_cli.py.

[1/1] Plan: commit the companion ADR-012 proposal for using lattice as neurocore's research evidence backend, with the MCP tool inventory corrected to all 21 advertised tools

impact_assessment.why: The working tree carries an untracked-in-time ADR mirroring neurocore ADR-007. It was missing the neighbors tool from the zero-detail-loss inventory, so committing it unchanged would make the proposed contract incomplete.
impact_assessment.benefits: Keeps both projects' integration proposals aligned, records the Proposed status and stdlib-only constraint, and gives the future adapter work a single reviewable contract.
impact_assessment.risks: Docs only: no runtime, dependency or state change. The proposal is not implemented, and saying so avoids implying the API module exists.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Verify the tool list against lattice.mcp.TOOLS, keep Status Proposed, and run python aikit.py check lattice before committing.
